claim_scope: For the exact installed runtime versions and exercised interfaces, provider outcomes describe native runtime behavior and Conduit outcomes describe the adapter/lifecycle boundary. Each cell links runtime receipts and, where used, current source/test evidence. This is implementation and local qualification evidence, not independent terminal qualification or universal compatibility.

non_claims: No universal interoperability claim is made.
No existing operator provider session was listed globally, read, adopted, prompted, interrupted, archived, or stopped.
Provider completion, task completion, verification, and objective acceptance are not inferred from one another.
Provider identity is not Conduit task identity; provider host, session/thread, turn, and writer authority remain separate.
Permission awareness and nonempty file diff/artifact telemetry remain unknown unless a live provider event/artifact was observed.
Gemini authentication was not invoked even though key presence and ACP-advertised methods were recorded as non-secret booleans/IDs.
Antigravity authentication and conversation cleanup were not attempted because no safe read-only auth status and exact-session deletion path were exposed by the inspected CLI help.
Shell process-group visibility is not a claim of complete arbitrary descendant cleanup; tmux and direct PTY release semantics differ.
No active provider turn was left running across release_supervision; active-turn continuation after release remains unknown for OpenCode, Codex, and Grok.

OpenCode cancel_active_turn support is bounded to an accepted abort request with observed busy-to-idle cessation/session.idle; the tested interface exposed no exact turn ID or explicit terminal cancellation reason.
